To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) patient education and home blood pressure monitoring (HBPM) is an effective way to improve hypertension control, medication compliance and lifestyle behaviors; 2) patient education and HBPM is an effective way of increasing the awareness of the importance of lifestyle behaviors and weight loss in hypertension management; and, 3) patient education and HPM is an effective method to improve the knowledge of hypertension and medication compliance.

the effect of a structured patient education program, with or without home monitoring, on patient compliance, blood pressure control, lifestyle behaviours and body mass index was not significantly better than usual care in a primary health setting.
patient education, home monitoring, and a nurse-led intervention can improve medication compliance, hypertension control, and lifestyle behaviours in primary care.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of patient education on medication compliance, blood pressure control, lifestyle behaviour and weight in patients with hypertension in a primary health-care setting.
the effect of patient education on hypertension management and medication compliance.
the effect of patient education on the management of hypertension, and on healthy lifestyle behaviours and body mass index (BMI) in patients with primary hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is no evidence that patient education and home blood pressure monitoring has any significant impact on patient medication compliance, hypertension control, healthy lifestyle behaviours or body mass index in the primary health care setting, and that the current evidence is insufficient to support its use in this setting.
there is a strong positive correlation between the amount of education a person has and the likelihood of that person being in good health, and that there is no evidence of a negative correlation.
patient education is a very important factor in improving medication compliance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patient education, self-monitoring and follow up in a primary health centre setting can improve patient knowledge and self-care behaviour and lead to improved clinical outcomes.

the patient education and home BP monitoring intervention improved medication adherence, blood pressure management, and healthy lifestyles, but not BMI, and that the effect was greater for those with lower levels of education.
the patient education and home blood pressure monitoring intervention improved medication compliance, healthy lifestyle behaviours, hypertension management and BMI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is an opportunity for the healthcare system to do a better job of supporting patients with hypertension, especially in terms of medication adherence.
the use of a digital health tool can improve medication adherence in patients with hypertension.
patient education is important for the management of hypertension, but the effect of home monitoring on medication adherence, hypertension management, and lifestyle behaviors is not clear.
